# Format Bank (Woodworking), Modifiers, and Word Banks

Every format below is proven by view data (see `reference-titles.md`). Generate by pairing these formats with proven woodworking topics and the right channel persona. **Do not invent new formats** — extend this bank only from new winning data.

**F-numbers are shared with the plumbing-ideation bank** so logic transfers between the two systems. Examples here are woodworking. Formats that transfer weakly to woodworking (e.g., F31 family-emergency, F20 disgust/causal-horror) are omitted below — if a woodworking topic ever supplies the raw material, pull them from the plumbing skill's bank. Two woodworking-native formats (F36, F37) are added at the end.

## Table of contents
1. Core transferable formats (with woodworking examples)
2. Woodworking-native formats (F36–F37)
3. Modifier families
4. Word banks
5. Structure skeletons
6. Channel-persona notes on format choice

---

## 1. Core transferable formats

- **F1 — The NEVER warning.** "NEVER Put These 7 Finishes on a Cutting Board (They're NOT Food-Safe!)" / "7 Wood Joints You Should NEVER Use". Prohibition + implied disaster. Works as a clean single clause.
- **F2 — Veteran authority / persona prevention.** "In 40 Years at the Bench, I've NEVER Thrown Away a Single Offcut — Here's Why" / "In 50 Years of Woodworking, These 10 Jigs Saved Me the Most Time". Credibility claimed in voiceover; perfect for faceless. Strongest on Dale and Sawdust Sam.
- **F3 — Numbered SECRETS/TIPS + THOUSANDS.** "15 GENIUS Shop Jigs That Will Save You THOUSANDS" / "25 GENIUS Woodworking Tips You NEED To Know". The infinitely repeatable listicle engine — escalate the number over time (12 → 15 → 20 → 25). The operator's own two winners are this format.
- **F4 — Insider betrayal.** "The Table Saw Upgrade Master Woodworkers NEVER Talk About" / "The Caulking Trick That Makes Cheap Trim Look PROFESSIONAL". Positions the persona as the honest insider breaking ranks.
- **F5 — Universal claim.** "The GENIUS Trick That Hides ANY Ugly Gap in Your Woodworking". Also the footage cheat code: universal methods justify generic compiled b-roll.
- **F6 — Ego challenge.** "I BET You're Cutting Wood WRONG — 10 Mistakes Every Beginner Makes". Confrontational knowledge-gap hook. Matches the channels' confirmed beginner skew.
- **F7 — Versus + test.** "[Tool A] vs [Tool B] — Which One ACTUALLY Cuts Cleaner?" Product/method debate; audiences have tribal opinions. Note: "I tested" only works as a persona verdict for faceless, not a filmed experiment.
- **F7b — Naked decision versus.** Plain, undecorated purchase-moment versus (e.g., "Track Saw vs Table Saw"). High-intent search queries need no hype and monetize best — don't over-decorate.
- **F8 — Pre-purchase gate.** "Watch This BEFORE You Spend Thousands on Woodworking Tools". Money-loss variant of the buying-gate; high-intent, monetizes well. (Proven in the ecosystem: "Watch This Before You Spend Thousands on Flooring" — 543k.)
- **F9 — Failure prophecy / mistakes.** "10 Woodworking Mistakes You Need To STOP Making (And What To Do Instead)" / "10 Trim Mistakes You Need to Stop Making". Fear + stakes; mistakes listicles outperform straight tutorials.
- **F10 — Diagnostic.** "Why Your [joint/finish/cut] Keeps [failing] — The Real Cause…". Why-your-X-does-Y. Pairs naturally with an F4 suffix.
- **F11 — Qualified how-to.** "…the RIGHT Way", "From SCRATCH", "the Easiest Way Possible", "(Beginner's Guide)". Example: "How To Repair a Terribly Damaged Door Jamb the Easiest Way Possible" (875k).
- **F12 — Effort minimization.** "How To Fix Ugly, Gappy Trim the Easiest Way Possible". Promises ease, not correction — a friendlier trigger than "you're doing it wrong". Needs a job people believe is hard.
- **F13 — Cost substitution.** "[Expensive tool/finish] Is Expensive. Do This Instead" / "10 Cheap Tools That BEAT Expensive Ones". Skip the paid option entirely.
- **F14 — Regret of ignorance.** "Woodworking Hacks You'll Wish You Knew Sooner". Sympathetic sibling of F6 — same gap, warmer tone.
- **F15 — Scarcity alternatives.** "When You Don't Have a [tool], Try These 3 Alternatives". Situational + listicle.
- **F16 — Concrete benchmark.** A vivid physical standard instead of an adjective ("joints TIGHT enough to hold without glue").
- **F17 — Problem-question opener.** "Bad Miter Joints? / Gappy Trim? / Blotchy Stain?" Opens by naming the viewer's exact problem as a question — instant self-selection. Title in the viewer's **sensory vocabulary** (what it looks like), not the technical cause.
- **F18 — Quantified micro-solution.** "How To Make Bad Miter Joints Look FLAWLESS in 60 Seconds". Tiny time + tiny cost; specific constraints make the mystery credible.
- **F19 — Lost wisdom / suppression / old-school.** "Old School Tricks That Make TERRIBLE Mitres Look PERFECT" (1.5m). The channels' biggest lever after listicles. **Sawdust Sam's home run** — he IS the old-timer, so run the honest version ("The Hand-Tool Trick Furniture Makers Used Before Power Tools"). Strong on Master Kenji in an Eastern key ("The Japanese Method the West Forgot").
- **F21 — The banned/no-longer-done explainer.** "The REAL Reason No One Builds Furniture This Way Anymore". Every dry rule or abandoned method is a hidden scandal. Needs a real rule/practice.
- **F22 — The in-group secret.** Third-person F2: "Why Master Woodworkers' Own Furniture Never Falls Apart — The Joint They Always Use". High confidence.
- **F23 — Mechanism mystery.** Counted-but-unnamed components ("The Two Cheap Tools That Replace Half Your Shop"); "which two?" is a stronger itch than a named tool. Small numbers exempt from the listicle-length rule.
- **F24 — "…And Watch What Happens."** "Pour Glue Into Sawdust and Watch What Happens". The inverted tease: gives the method, hides the outcome.
- **F25 — N uses compendium.** "20 GENIUS Things To Do With Sawdust You'd NEVER Think Of" / "13 Things You Can Do With Sawdust" (357k). Substance/material as protagonist, breadth promise. Pairs with F26.
- **F26 — Never throw away X.** "You'll NEVER Throw Away Sawdust Again After Watching This" / "Stop Throwing Away Offcuts". Behavior-change prophecy. In woodworking this is strong (scrap/offcuts/sawdust are the biggest validated cluster), unlike its weak plumbing transfer.
- **F27 — Like never before / performance restoration.** "Make Your [dull tool] Cut Like New Again". Enhancement framing — the tool works but could be better than ever. The unserved middle between "broken" and "fine".
- **F28 — Survivor shortlist.** "The Only 5 Power Tools a Beginner Woodworker REALLY Needs". Extreme-filter buying guide. "Only N" stays small — scarcity is the hook.
- **F29 — The grade lie / quality exposé.** "Why Modern Furniture Falls Apart in 5 Years (The Particleboard Lie)". Statistical doom + present-progressive decay + a named deception. **Sawdust Sam's second home run** (built-to-last vs disposable). Honest ammunition is abundant.
- **F30 — Hidden asset reframe.** "Turn ONE Cheap 2x4 Into 7 Projects That Look EXPENSIVE" — you already own/can-cheaply-buy the solution in disguise.
- **F32 — The truth about X.** "The TRUTH About Mineral Oil on Cutting Boards (You've Been Lied To)". Myth-busting; honest-fit targets: mineral oil, "food-safe" finish myths, biscuit strength, exotic-wood necessity.
- **F33 — STOP doing the default.** "Stop Using Mineral Oil on Your Cutting Boards — Do THIS Instead" / "Stop Building Birdhouses Like THIS" (161k) / "Stop Using Your Table Saw Until You Add These 10 Upgrades". NEVER prohibits; STOP commands cessation of the current behavior, then substitutes.
- **F34 — Precise savings opener.** "Save $400 Building Your Own [X] — Here's How". Exact dollar figure first; the specific mid-size number is the credibility sweet spot between THOUSANDS and $1.
- **F35 — The recurrence problem.** "Why Your [finish/joint/cut] Keeps [failing] and How to STOP It". Chronic problems: blotchy stain, joints that keep loosening, tearout that keeps happening. "THIS" enables title-thumbnail interlock.

## 2. Woodworking-native formats (F36–F37)

*New formats discovered from woodworking ecosystem data. Add future woodworking-native formats here as F38+.*

- **F36 — First-person contrarian dismissal.** "I Don't Get Why ANYONE Still Uses These Woodworking Joints" (3.3m — the single biggest outlier in the pool). The persona openly can't understand why people still do the common thing; part hot-take, part gentle shaming, part "there's a better way you don't know". Reads as an authentic opinion, not a listicle. Needs a genuinely debatable common practice (pocket holes, certain joints, a popular tool, a finishing habit). Strong on all three personas; on Master Kenji it becomes "why the West still does X the hard way".
- **F37 — Amateur / pro divide.** "7 Woodworking Skills That Separate Amateurs From PROS" / "3 Baseboard Skills that Separate Amateurs from Pros" (2m). Sorts the viewer into a tier and promises the crossover skills. Sibling of F6 (ego) and F29 (grade lie) but distinct — the hook is the visible skill gap and the aspiration to cross it. "Master" is on-brand for Master Kenji ("…Separate Amateurs from MASTERS").

## 3. Modifier families (attach to any format)

- **Parentheticals** — use the flavor that kills the viewer's specific doubt:
  - Objection-killer: "(No Special Tools)", "(No Table Saw)", "(No Experience Needed)"
  - Adversary tag: "(Woodworking Stores Hate This)", "(The Pros Never Mention It)"
  - Credibility tag: "(Beginner's Guide)", "(40 Years of Pro Tips!)", "(The Japanese Way)"
  - Surprise tease: "(The Results Will SURPRISE You!)"
  - Insider-term/loophole: "(The Particleboard Lie)", "(The Supply-Grade Secret)" — teaching the trade's vocabulary is itself a hook
  - Guilt hook: "(You're Probably Doing It)", "(You're Wasting a Goldmine)"
  - Value verdict: "(Worth It!)", "(And 5 to Skip)", "(Total Waste of Money)"
- **Urgency:** Before Your Next Project, This Weekend, Right Now, Before You Buy Anything Else, Before Winter.
- **Totality/whole-shop:** Every Project, EVERY Cut, Completely, ALL.
- **Permanence/certainty:** FOREVER, PERMANENTLY, GUARANTEED, Never Again, Lasts Generations.
- **Effort negation (stackable):** No Table Saw, No Power Tools, No Fancy Jigs, No Experience, No Mess. Staccato delivery proven: "No Nails. No Glue."
- **Named-retailer/lumber anchor:** "Using Only Wood From Lowe's", "One $5 Board From Home Depot" — folksy ultra-concreteness. **Native to Dale; avoid on Master Kenji and Sawdust Sam**, whose personas reject big-box/disposable framing.
- **Money-loss present tense:** "That's Costing You Money", "Is Ruining Your Furniture", "You're Wasting" — loss happening now, not hypothetically.
- **Sells/value framing:** "That SELL for Stupid Money", "That Look Like You Spent THOUSANDS" — the make-money and look-expensive angles both proven on scrap topics.
- **Title-thumbnail interlock:** "THIS" in the title forces the thumbnail to complete the meaning; neither spoils alone. Proven in the pool ("Stop Building Birdhouses Like THIS").

## 4. Word banks

- **Caps-worthy power words:** NEVER, STOP, SECRET(S), GENIUS, THOUSANDS, FREE, GUARANTEED, FOREVER, ANY, ALL, EVERY, FATAL, BANNED, REAL, TRUTH, ACTUALLY, WRONG, PRO(S), MASTER, AMAZING, PERFECT, FLAWLESS, EXPENSIVE, WORTH IT.
- **Lost-wisdom vocabulary:** old-school, old-timers, before power tools, the way it's always been done, still unbeaten, grandpa's, swore by, generations. (Sawdust Sam's native register.)
- **Precision/mastery vocabulary (Master Kenji):** razor-sharp, dead-flat, no nails, no glue, hairline, the Japanese way, the secret the West never learned, mirror finish.
- **Exclusivity ladder (climb as needed):** Most beginners get this wrong → Pros don't talk about it → Nobody teaches → NO ONE knows about → The industry pretends it doesn't exist.
- **Adversary roster:** big-box furniture makers ("particleboard"/"flat-pack"), tool marketers, "the woodworking stores", brand manufacturers, the modern disposable-furniture industry. The persona is the honest exception.
- **Money language by scale:** FREE (terminal point) → $1 / $5 micro-cost (native to Dale) → Save $400-style exact figures → THOUSANDS (vague-big stakes). "Built to last generations" and "worth every penny" are the value-not-cheap register for Sam and Kenji. Use one scale per title.
- **Sensory/quality symptom words:** blotchy, tearout, wobbly, gappy, split, warped, dull, racking, ugly gaps.
- **Material/behavior protagonists:** sawdust, offcuts, scrap, a single 2x4, one board — proven to carry a title on their own.

## 5. Structure skeletons (mirror these shapes; vary across a batch)

- Single-clause listicle: "7 Wood Joints You Should NEVER Use (And What Pros Use Instead)"
- Listicle + payoff: "15 GENIUS Shop Jigs That Will Save You THOUSANDS (Build Them in Minutes)"
- Persona two-part: "In 40 Years at the Bench, I've Never [X] — Here's Exactly What I [Do/Use]"
- STOP substitution: "Stop [default] — [the better way]" ("Stop Using Mineral Oil on Your Cutting Boards — Do THIS Instead")
- Contrarian dismissal (F36): "I Don't Get Why ANYONE Still [common practice]"
- Amateur/pro (F37): "[N] [Skills/Mistakes] That Separate Amateurs From PROS"
- Question opener + fix: "Gappy Trim? The Easiest Fix Possible (No Special Tools)"
- Value verdict: "[Category] Tools Beginners ACTUALLY Need (And [N] to Skip)"
- Make-money / look-expensive: "[N] Scrap Wood Projects That [SELL for Stupid Money / Look Like You Spent THOUSANDS]"
- Action tease (F24): "Pour [substance] Into Your [material] and Watch What Happens"
- Never-throw-away (F26): "You'll NEVER Throw Away [material] Again After Watching This"

## 6. Channel-persona notes on format choice

- **Dale Oakfield's Workshop:** the full bank. Big-box/cheap-lumber anchors, beginner-mistakes, tips listicles, tool-buying, jigs. Default when no channel is specified.
- **Master Kenji:** favor F19 (Eastern key), F36 ("why the West still…"), F37 ("…from MASTERS"), F22 (the joint masters always use), precision F5/F18, hand-tool F13/F28. Avoid big-box/$5-hack anchors. Register is mastery, not thrift.
- **Sawdust Sam:** favor F19 (lost wisdom — his strongest lane), F2 (veteran), F29 (quality-decline/built-to-last), F4 (insider), F21 (abandoned methods). Avoid big-box/disposable anchors. Register is heritage and durability, not cheapness or speed.
